description: A query parameter is interpolated into a shell command executed via exec, allowing attacker-controlled shell metacharacters to break out and run arbitrary commands.
remediation: Do not pass user input to exec. Use execFile or spawn with an arguments array, or remove the shell call. If shell use is required, strictly validate input (e.g., IP/hostname format) and reject anything else.
title: Command Injection via exec template literal in routes/search.js

judge.reason: Aggregated from MoA candidates that passed false-positive judging.

description: A user-controlled value is concatenated into a string passed to child_process.exec, allowing arbitrary command execution via shell metacharacters.
evidence: src/app.js lines 8-10: const tool = req.query.tool; return childProcess.exec("tool " + tool);
remediation: Replace exec with execFile or spawn that takes an argument array, avoiding shell interpretation. Validate input against an allowlist of permitted tool identifiers.
title: Command Injection via exec with query parameter in app.js

judge.reason: Aggregated from MoA candidates that passed false-positive judging.

description: User-controlled input from a query parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL query string, enabling SQL injection.
evidence: src/app.js lines 3-5: const term = req.query.q; return db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + term + "'");
remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements so user input is bound, not interpolated, into the SQL command.
title: SQL Injection via unsanitized query parameter in app.js
